name: @shikijs/magic-move
notes: 2026-11-01: Shiki-highlighted code-state transitions; replaces the archived shiki-magic-move package.
2026-11-01: Licence as reported by the source research, not yet verified: MIT.
2026-11-01: CSS transitions are not seekable; needs a frame-seekable adapter and odiff gating before promotion.
2026-11-01: Captured from research report; listed-in-prd is the schema's listed-only status. Version and maintenance not yet assessed.
2026-11-01: Triage: assess. Report rates it a strong candidate.

2026-11-15: @shikijs/magic-move 4.6.0 published 2026-11-11 (npm reported four days before assessment). Former shiki-magic-move repository archived 2026-06-03; since v4.2.0 it re-exports the maintained package. Seekable animation/capture behavior not validated.

2026-11-24: Evidence used @shikijs/magic-move 4.6.0 with shiki 4.6.0, not the archived shiki-magic-move 1.4.0 npm package. Transitions are CSS; the fixture pauses them and seeks currentTime per frame. Shiki-tokenised runs only; no WebGL, wrappers or encoding.

2026-11-24: Toolkit guide written at skills/shikijs-magic-move/SKILL.md from the shiki-magic-move-capture evidence; sizes the scene to the library duration option and freezes transitions via the seek route.

evidence.result: 90 alpha frames at 1280x720 (Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Playwright 1.64.1, Node 22.19.0): 61 distinct hashes; shuffled equals sequential; frame 0 equals static A, frame 89 equals static B; frame 45 differs from both, alpha min 0 max 1. Second run after a timeline amendment; the first run failed the middle-frame check because the transition had settled by 1.0 s (README).
evidence.scope: Magic Move DOM renderer, CSS transitions frozen per seek; one TS snippet pair, github-dark, JetBrains Mono; alpha PNG; macOS arm64. Not other wrappers, themes, browsers or encodes.

summary: @shikijs/magic-move turns Shiki-highlighted code states into animated diffs, with framework wrappers and a precompiled-token path; unlike ordinary code highlighting, it includes token matching and transition rendering.
use_when: When code-state transitions are the focus of a scene
When syntax-highlighted snippets need token-aware diffs
When code states can be precompiled and supplied as steps
avoid_when: When transitions must be fully seekable without a custom capture strategy

assessment.rationale: The maintained package is @shikijs/magic-move; npm reports 4.6.0 published four days before assessment and MIT. Upstream says the old shiki-magic-move repo is archived and a thin re-export since v4.2.0; future work is in shikijs/shiki. It offers precompiled token steps, though seekable capture still needs a deterministic route.
